solutions.check: clues read from the FT's printable PDF (PDF has no vector grid), the grid backsolved from their numbering, the one grid that fits; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Run away often pursuing aide

definitions.meaning: to bolt or leave in a hurry, as an army striking camp
in the military title aide-..., the last two parts regularly follow the word aide

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: in 'aide-de-camp' the word wanted comes straight after 'aide', so it is often found pursuing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off suddenly or secretly is the core meaning of this verb.

clue.text: Object of batting with glance at cover

parts.note: to eye something is to glance at it
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A cricketer's shot is described as something done with a quick look towards the cover fielders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batting' and 'cover' (a fielding position) suggest cricket, but the batting is the fluttering of lashes.
explanation.definitionFit: People bat their lashes by flapping this fold of skin, so it is what gets batted.

clue.text: A meagre surrounding to finish on the up and up

indicators.note: the word for meagre is placed around the word for finish

parts.note: scant means meagre
end means finish

explanation.surface: A thin border finishing a design is said to be rising steadily.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rising in power or influence is described as climbing, on the up and up.

clue.text: Tenor and former soprano absorbing heart from Navarone

indicators.note: the singer's name takes the central letters of the film title into itself

parts.note: Adelina Patti was a celebrated nineteenth-century soprano

indicators.note: the central letters of Navarone are taken

explanation.surface: A tenor and a retired soprano take on a role from the war film The Guns of Navarone.
explanation.definitionFit: Luciano Pavarotti was the most famous operatic tenor of his age.

clue.text: Sum thing wrong? I can arm you

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are set wrongly, out of order

explanation.surface: Someone offers to supply weapons after a sum has gone awry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the eight letters of SUM THING.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes and repairs firearms can equip you with weapons.

clue.text: Celebration enjoyed by K

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
had, as in had a good time, means enjoyed

explanation.surface: A party that was savoured by someone called K.
explanation.walkthrough: K is the chess abbreviation for king, but throughout this puzzle it stands for knight, here a Round Table knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad is the purest knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: The black country?

parts.note: the Latin word for black names an African nation; the Black Country is also a region of the English Midlands

explanation.walkthrough: The Black Country is an industrial area near Birmingham, but the clue wants a country whose name is Latin for black.
explanation.definitionFit: This West African state's name echoes the Latin word for black.

clue.text: Setter married and confined

parts.note: the crossword setter refers to himself as me
wed means married

explanation.surface: A dog breed, the setter, has married and is now cooped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the dog, but in crosswords it is the compiler, giving ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawks were kept shut in a mews, so to be mewed up is to be shut away.

clue.text: K to stir trouble with car

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so the letters of stir are disturbed

parts.note: a tram is a car running on rails

explanation.surface: A knight sets out to cause trouble with a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Tristram, lover of Isolde, is a knight of the Round Table.

clue.text: Catholic quartet in ring for K

indicators.note: the abbreviations go inside the word for ring

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
RC is short for Roman Catholic
IV is the Roman numeral four

explanation.surface: A group of four Catholics in a circle look out for a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Percival is the Round Table knight of the Grail quest.

clue.text: K in Scotland absent in spirit

indicators.note: the Scottish word sits inside the word for spirit

parts.note: gin is a spirit
awa is the Scots form of away, absent

explanation.surface: A knight in Scotland is missing, though present in spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain, hero of the Green Knight poem, is a knight of the Round Table.

clue.text: Meal for one making a row?

definitions.meaning: the main meal of the day
read as din plus -ner, someone who makes a din, a row

explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' here rhymes with 'cow': a racket, or din, so a din-maker is a 'din-ner' in the punning reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal meal, usually eaten in the evening, goes by this name.

clue.text: This is where a heartless song finds transmission

parts.note: here means this place, where we are

indicators.note: the song loses one of its central letters

parts.note: a ditty is a simple song

explanation.surface: Someone explains where a song without feeling is passed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops one of the two middle Ts of DITTY, leaving DITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologists speak of the passing down of traits from parents to offspring, their genetic transmission.

clue.text: Very old valetudinarian without a right to go wrong

indicators.note: the remaining letters are made to go wrong, scrambled
the word sheds the two letters named

explanation.surface: An elderly hypochondriac, lacking any right, is about to go astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A and R from VALETUDINARIAN; 'to go wrong' rearranges the twelve letters left. A valetudinarian is a person anxious about their health.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally 'before the Flood', this adjective means extremely old or old-fashioned.

clue.text: Not bound to loiter around centre of Moseley

indicators.note: the word for loiter goes round the central letters

parts.note: to loaf is to loiter idly

indicators.note: all but the end letters of Moseley are taken

explanation.surface: Someone hangs about in the middle of Moseley, a Birmingham suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pages held in a ring binder rather than stitched into a spine are not bound.

clue.text: Porch oddly built in — vide! (see, translated)

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: v. is the abbreviation of vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: the letters of see are transformed, put in another arrangement
the letters of built are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A porch is oddly constructed, with a scholarly note telling the reader to see a translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' turns BUILT into TIBUL; 'translated' turns SEE into ESE; TIBUL then goes into V plus ESE.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance hall or porch leading into a building is called by this name.

clue.text: Unimportant, in fact grotty and taken away, a badge of office

indicators.note: a set of letters is removed from the long word

parts.note: insignificant means unimportant
the letters of in fact, made grotty or shoddy, come out in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A badge of office is dismissed as trivial, in fact shabby, and is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grotty' rearranges IN FACT into FICANT, and 'taken away' removes those letters from INSIGNIFICANT, leaving INSIGNI; A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Emblems or badges worn to show rank or office are known by this Latin plural.

clue.text: Unconvincing note to leave in an acceptance that it's a free-for-all?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the three pieces sit inside the word of acceptance

parts.note: yes is a word of acceptance
a thin excuse is unconvincing
G is a musical note
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A weak memo about departing is taken as admitting there are no rules.
explanation.definitionFit: This stock phrase says no rules or limits apply, a free-for-all.

clue.text: K drops in to make acquisition

indicators.note: the word for drops goes inside the other

parts.note: to get is to acquire
rain falls in drops

explanation.surface: A knight drops by to pick something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' looks like a verb with 'in', but it is the noun, RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Geraint, husband of Enid, is one of King Arthur's knights.

clue.text: K chewing the rag

indicators.note: chewing mangles the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A knight is having a long grumble, chewing the rag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chewing the rag' is British slang for chatting or arguing at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gareth, brother of Gawain, is a knight of the Round Table.

clue.text: Transparent stuff by second missing composer for Dickensian optimist

parts.note: mica is a mineral that splits into clear sheets

indicators.note: the composer's name loses its second letter

parts.note: Carl Maria von Weber was a German composer

explanation.surface: Clear material beside a composer who is absent describes a cheerful character from Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Micawber in David Copperfield always trusts that something will turn up.

clue.text: Jelly as a film?

parts.note: a pic is an informal word for a film

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a jelly might serve as a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury jelly made from meat stock is known by this name.

clue.text: Girl of stone

definitions.meaning: a gem mineral, of which emerald is a variety

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a woman's name and a precious mineral of the gem family.

clue.text: What did you say about jail break — for profit, did you say?

indicators.note: the query word goes round the scrambled letters

parts.note: eh is what you say when you didn't catch something

indicators.note: the letters of jail are broken up

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a jailbreak was done for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' turns JAIL into LIJA. The definition is a sound-alike: 'profit, did you say?' means prophet, and Elijah was an Old Testament prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical figure carried up in a chariot of fire was a prophet, which sounds like profit.

clue.text: It's a certainty the Queen is one with a gun

parts.note: a snip is British slang for a sure thing or bargain
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Royalty is surely armed.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman who shoots from cover is a gunman of a particular kind.

clue.text: Diamonds greatly increase in value as rocks

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
to cube a number raises it to its third power, a big increase

explanation.surface: Gems that appreciate sharply are described as rocks, slang for jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' suggests diamonds, but it means what goes in a drink served on the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink on the rocks is served over these frozen blocks.

clue.text: Weapon destiny for K?

parts.note: a lance is a knight's weapon
one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: A knight's arms and fate are weighed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot, Guinevere's lover, is the best-known Round Table knight.

clue.text: Architectural addition unsuitable for vegetarians, say?

definitions.text: Architectural addition unsuitable for vegetarians, say?

parts.words: Architectural addition unsuitable for vegetarians, say?
parts.note: a slender church spire whose French name sounds like flesh, meat that vegetarians avoid

explanation.walkthrough: The French word for arrow names a slim spire, and its sound is close to 'flesh'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender spire, often over a church crossing, carries this French name.
